identification.summary: puNK-003 is a cluster name used by S2W's TALON team for activity it links to North Korea; the "puNK" prefix denotes a partially unidentified group [S1]. TALON analyzed an LNK file found on 2024-04-24, disguised as a tax-evasion report document, that drops and displays a decoy, then downloads an AutoIt script and a legitimate AutoIt3 interpreter from a hardcoded attacker server; the script runs a reimplementation of the Lilith RAT in AutoIt [S1]. S2W reported similarities to the KONNI group in obfuscation, PowerShell usage and AutoIt use, but differences too: here the LNK acts as a downloader, whereas KONNI's LNK malware acts as a dropper [S1].
identification.firstObserved: 2024-04 (LNK sample discovered by S2W TALON on 2024-04-24; earlier activity not established in sources reviewed) [S1]
identification.notes: The existing record also names a C++ Lilith RAT and the AutoIt variant CURKON; those details came from aggregator text (Malpedia/Strobes) that could not be fetched in this session and are not independently confirmed here. KONNI is a separate cluster; S2W noted similarities only, so facts are not merged [S1].

sources.title: Threat Analysis: Examination of puNK-003's Lilith RAT Converted to AutoIt Script (seen via search-result summary)

provenance.importedSummary: puNK-003 is a North Korean APT group known for deploying the Lilith RAT, a sophisticated C++ remote access trojan, and its AutoIt variant, CURKON, which functions as a downloader. The group primarily distributes malware through targeted phishing attacks using malicious LNK files. Analysis indicates that puNK-003 shares similarities with the KONNI group, particularly in the use of AutoIt scripts and specific coding functions. Key indicators of infection include unusual network activity and system slowdowns, with removal methods involving specialized antivirus software and manual techniques.
